caution: A failure to reproduce is not a finding that the paper is wrong. It may be a failure of the attempt.

attempts.label: DANDI:001525
attempts.paper_title: Sub-microsecond optical measurements of cell membrane charging and lesioning by pulsed electric fields
attempts.entry_title: Membrane recovery after 1-us electroporation (Semenov et al. 2026)
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Semenov et al. (2026) that dandiset 001525 can test. The dandiset holds the two-pulse strobe imaging of ten Di-8-ANEPPS-loaded CHO cells, a conditioning pulse followed by a 150 V/cm test pulse, the experiment of the paper's Fig. 7A and the bottom panel of Fig. 7B. The notebook measures the test-pulse polarization around each cell's perimeter and at its poles, and computes the conductivity calibration of Eq. (2). The other experiments of the paper are not in the dandiset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Semenov et al. (2026) from dandiset 001525

outcomes.statement: After a conditioning pulse of up to 1000 V/cm, polarization by the 150 V/cm test pulse 5 us later still follows a cosine of the angle to the field, while 1200 and 1400 V/cm conditioning pulses markedly reduce charging at the cell poles.
outcomes.quote: Polarization still followed a cosine function after conditioning PEFs of up to 1000 V/cm. However, 1200 and 1400 V/cm conditioning PEFs markedly hindered charging by the test pulse at cell poles, indicating a persistent membrane permeabilization.
outcomes.notes: After the first verification round the membrane trace was corrected. The overlays of the data check show that the first round's trace, the plain intensity peak along each ray, fell on bright dye inside cells c5 and c9 (a median 11.7 and 8.9 px inside the cell's outer edge); the trace used now is the intensity peak within 8 px inside the outer edge (2.5 to 4.8 px inside it in every cell). With it the outcome changes from partially reproduced to reproduced. Under the main reading (edge trace, six 5-us cells, annulus background, dark frames dropped), with the unpaired test of the amended criterion no pole reading differs from the 150/150 benchmark after 360 to 1000 V/cm conditioning (smallest p 0.059, mean of poles at 1000 V/cm), so the cosine part holds under reading (b). Pole dF is below the benchmark after 1200 and 1400 V/cm at the cathodic pole (unpaired p 0.022 and 0.0010) and for the mean of both poles (p 0.0013 and 0.0002); the anodic pole reaches p 0.086 at 1200 V/cm. Cosine amplitudes are 12.6% dF (benchmark), 10.4% (1000 V/cm) and 5.0% (1400 V/cm), R^2 0.73, 0.68 and -0.55 (A cos(theta - phi) without an offset term). Reading (a), the s.e. band, fails in every variant, and under the main reading at both poles at the control and at 1000 V/cm, because the profiles carry a uniform negative offset (-4.3% dF at the control); the baseline images fade by about 0.10% per frame in 43 of 44 files, which predicts -5.16% over all files against a measured -3.67% (r 0.18 over files), the sign of the bleaching the paper reports (Results 3.2) but not its size, so the offset's source is not established. With an offset term, a diagnostic outside the criterion, the fit lies within the s.e. at both poles up to 1000 V/cm and not at 1200 or 1400 V/cm. Over 22 variants the claim holds in 19; it fails in the 3 with the first round's peak trace, where the 1200 V/cm hindrance is not significant at any pole, so the 19 are not independent confirmations; the outcome turns on the edge trace. With the paired test, a variant, it holds in 21 of 22. The window of the edge trace (8 px) is a choice; with all six cells the claim holds under every window from 4 to 12 px (hindered at the cathodic pole and the mean of poles from 6 to 10 px, at every pole with 4 px, for the mean of poles only with 12 px). The trace of c5 dips into the cathodic pole arc in its 760 and 1000 V/cm files (8.8 and 8.2 px below its running median), strengths at which the cosine part holds; in c5's first file the notch lies 22 to 35 degrees from the cathodic pole. The outcome rests on the trace, the rank mapping of strengths and the single-pulse benchmark.
deviations: The perimeter trace is found automatically, where the paper draws "the 6-pixel-wide trace ... along the cell perimeter" by hand in MetaMorph (Methods 2.3). The membrane at each angle is the intensity peak within 8 px inside the cell's outer edge (the steepest outward fall of intensity), an assumption adopted after the first round's plain intensity peak was seen to fall inside two cells; that trace is shown as a variant, and so are windows of 4, 6, 10 and 12 px.
The analysed cell is the largest object in each subject's field (an assumption; the paper says one cell per experiment, Fig. 2 legend, and does not say how it was chosen).

The field direction in image coordinates is not given by the dataset; it is the A-weighted circular mean of cosine-fit phases over all 5-us files (-75.6 degrees, per-file sd 6.8), and from the control files alone as a variant (-73.9 degrees). 0 degrees is the depolarized pole, as Fig. 7A plots it.

Conditioning strengths are mapped by rank from the files' generator volts (100 to 350 V) to the Fig. 7A labels 360 to 1400 V/cm, and the single 50 V pulse, recorded first in every cell, is taken as the 150/150 benchmark; an assumption, as the files give no field strengths and no 150/150 pair. Read as steps of 100 V from 0.15 kV/cm at 50 V, the strengths in the files' general description would put the levels 0 to 11% lower, with the same order.
Six 5-us cells are in the dataset where the paper reports n = 5; all six are used, and each five-cell subset is shown.

Background and dark frames are open in the paper. Main reading adopted as an assumption, background removed (median of an annulus 1.6 to 2.2 radii) and frames without a laser flash dropped; the paper's own scale (Fig. 7A about 13% dF at 150/150; 9.1% dF per 100 mV in Results 3.3, about 16% dF at 150 V/cm) is met only with a background removed (12.6 to 12.9% against 5.6%), and the files' camera floor is about 209 counts under a membrane trace of 451 to 692. All four combinations are shown.

The criterion's pole dF is tested under the pole readings of fig7b-test-pulse-unchanged-to-760 (cathodic, anodic, mean of both), with its test, the unpaired two-sample t-test against the control group (the paired test shown as a variant); reading (a) compares the fit at each pole with the s.e. of the pole mean over cells, for the legend's gray outline.

outcomes.statement: Polarization by the test pulse 6 us after the conditioning pulse does not differ from the undamaged control for conditioning pulses up to 760 V/cm, and is at about 80% of control after 1000 V/cm, a difference that is not significant.
outcomes.quote: measurements 6 μs later (test pulse) did not differ from the control up to 760 V/cm strength of the conditioning PEF; they were at ~80% of the control reading after 1000 V/cm conditioning PEF but the difference was not statistically significant
outcomes.notes: The earlier run blocked this claim as methods_underspecified, because the criterion then required it when the paired and unpaired tests disagree, and they did. The reader's answer (questions/001525.yaml) amended the criterion to take the unpaired two-sample t-test against the control group as the paper's test, with the paired and one-sample tests as variants, and dropped that rule. After the first verification round the membrane trace was corrected (see fig7a-test-pulse-cosine-up-to-1000); the outcome stays reproduced. Under the main reading the unpaired t-test finds no difference from control at 360 to 1000 V/cm at either pole (smallest p 0.098, anodic at 760 V/cm; cathodic p 0.21 to 0.99). The absence holds in 19 of 22 variants; in the other 3 the anodic pole differs at 760 V/cm (p 0.027 to 0.046). At 1000 V/cm the test response is 79.7% of control at the anodic pole, within 80 +- 8, the measured value recorded as the only pole reading that matches; it is 57.5% at the cathodic pole and 71.9% for their mean, outside the tolerance (unpaired p 0.21 and 0.24). In all 22 variants at least one pole reading is within tolerance. Unpaired effect sizes up to 1000 V/cm run from d = -1.05 to +0.15. The paired test, a variant, finds no difference at either pole under the main reading (smallest p 0.098) and in 18 of 22 variants; the one-sample test in 21 of 22. For the mean of both poles, which the criterion does not test for absence, the paired test gives p 0.018 at 760 V/cm and 0.016 at 1000 V/cm (unpaired 0.14 and 0.059). The trace window changes the outcome; the absence holds with windows of 6 to 12 px and fails with 4 px (anodic pole at 760 V/cm, p 0.028), and without c5 it fails under every window (anodic 760 V/cm, p 0.010 to 0.046). The trace of c5 dips into the cathodic pole arc in its 760 and 1000 V/cm files, where its cathodic dF is -3.3% and -1.9%; these values pull the cathodic pole towards a difference, and none is found (unpaired p 0.74 and 0.21). With the first round's trace the cathodic pole was at 133% of control after 360 V/cm (paired p 0.0038); with the edge trace it is at 99.5%. The outcome rests on the trace and its window, the rank mapping of strengths and the single-pulse benchmark, assumptions shared with fig7a-test-pulse-cosine-up-to-1000.
deviations: Same trace, cell, field direction, strength mapping, benchmark, cell count and main reading as fig7a-test-pulse-cosine-up-to-1000.

outcomes.statement: Conditioning pulses of 1200 and 1400 V/cm reduce charging by the test pulse 6 us later to about 70% and 50% of control (p < 0.05 and p < 0.01).
outcomes.quote: Still more intense PEFs of 1200 and 1400 V/cm reduced charging by the test pulse to ~70% and ~ 50%, respectively (p < 0.05 and p < 0.01, two-sided t-test)
outcomes.notes: After the first verification round the membrane trace was corrected (see fig7a-test-pulse-cosine-up-to-1000), and the outcome changes from not reproduced to partially reproduced. Measured values are the cathodic pole, the first pole reading the criterion lists. Under the main reading both reductions reach the paper's significance levels at the cathodic pole (25.2% and -11.3% of control after 1200 and 1400 V/cm, unpaired p 0.022 and 0.0010) and for the mean of both poles (53.4% and 27.2%, p 0.0013 and 0.0002), with values outside 70 +- 7 and 50 +- 5, which the criterion calls partial. The anodic pole has values within tolerance (68.7% and 48.0%) but p 0.086 and 0.011, short of p < 0.05 and p < 0.01. No pole reading meets the whole criterion in any of 22 variants; both significance levels are reached in 19; in the 3 with the first round's peak trace no pole reading reaches both (not reproduced, the first round's outcome). The paired variant meets the whole criterion in none. Effect sizes at 1400 V/cm are -10.5% dF at the cathodic pole (unpaired d -2.66) and -9.1% dF at the anodic (d -1.80). The partial outcome comes from the cathodic and mean readings only. The round-2 verifier pointed out that Results 3.7 paragraph 6 omits a negative cathodic dF at 1400 V/cm; if that is the test-pulse value, the paper's ~50% can only be an anodic value. Under the anodic reading alone the values are within tolerance in 12 of 22 variants, both significance levels are reached in 2 and the whole criterion in none; under the main reading (p 0.086 and 0.011) the claim would be not reproduced. This is asked of a reader (questions/001525.yaml), and the outcome is judged on the criterion as written. The cathodic value after 1400 V/cm (-11.3%) is negative, as the omitted value is; after 1200 V/cm (25.2%) it lies well below the paper's 70%. Under every trace window from 4 to 12 px both significance levels are reached with values outside tolerance and the whole criterion is met under no pole reading; the anodic values stay within tolerance (67.3 to 69.2% and 43.6 to 48.3%) with p 0.035 to 0.092 at 1200 V/cm.
deviations: Same trace, cell, field direction, strength mapping, benchmark, cell count and main reading as fig7a-test-pulse-cosine-up-to-1000.

outcomes.statement: Under Eq. (2), effective membrane conductivity barely affects charging while it stays far below cytosol and medium conductivity; a 10-fold increase reduces IMP by about 2% and a 100-fold increase by 12%.
outcomes.quote: its 10-fold increase would go unnoticed, yielding just a ~2% IMP reduction, and a 100-fold increase would reduce IMP by just 12%
outcomes.notes: Eq. (2) with the Methods' parameters gives f = 1.498 for the intact membrane, an IMP reduction (1 - f/1.5) of 11.87% for a 100-fold rise in membrane conductivity, within 12 +- 1.2, and 1.33% for a 10-fold rise, outside 2 +- 0.5 (1.20% relative to the intact f). With R from 6 to 10 um the 10-fold value stays between 1.00% and 1.65%. The equation in the PDF's text layer (page 3) has the form the claims file read; the rendered page could not be viewed (no PDF renderer in this run either). The "~2%" may have been read from the Fig. 5B graph.

outcomes.statement: During the electroporating pulse, pole polarization falls below the linear scaling expected for an undamaged membrane, 1.5-fold below at 560 V/cm and 2-fold at 760 V/cm and further at stronger fields, significantly for every strength of 560 V/cm or more.
outcomes.quote: Actual measurements fell 1.5 times below this line for 560 V/cm PEFs ... and diverged further for more intense PEFs (p < 0.01 for all datapoints ≥560 V/cm, one sample t-test)
outcomes.notes: The top panel of Fig. 7B comes from the single-pulse escalation of Fig. 4B (Results 3.7, "Data for the top panel of Fig. 7B were extracted from dF measurements in Fig. 4B"). The dataset holds one image per pulse pair, at 900 ns into the test pulse, and single pulses only at 50 V (150 V/cm); no image of a conditioning pulse at 360 to 1400 V/cm is in it. The files' general description mentions single pulses from 0.15 to 1.57 kV/cm, which are not in this dandiset.

outcomes.statement: Effective membrane conductivity at the poles falls by about 10-fold (range 7 to 20) within 6 us after the electroporating pulse, for most datapoints.
outcomes.quote: Fig. 7C shows a profound reduction in the λm,eff within just 6 μs after the electroporating pulse. For most datapoints, it dropped by a factor of 10 (range: 7–20).
outcomes.notes: Depends on fig7b-conditioning-pulse-below-linear, whose conditioning-pulse images are not in the dataset. The test-pulse half (lm,eff from the test dF) could be computed from the dataset but the fold drop needs both.

outcomes.statement: After mildly electroporating pulses (570 and 760 V/cm) the membrane reseals fully within 6 us, while after stronger pulses increased conductivity persists for at least 6 us; the cathodic pole is more conductive than the anodic during the pulse, but the test pulse finds no difference between the poles.
outcomes.quote: While the cathodic pole became more conductive than the anodic pole during the electroporating pulse (Fig. 7B, see also Figs. 1 and 4B–D), no difference between the poles was detected by the test pulse. For mildly electroporating PEFs of 570 and 760 V/cm, membrane resealed fully (within the accuracy of measurements) within just 6 μs. With more intense PEFs, the residual increased conductivity persisted for at least 6 μs
outcomes.notes: The first round blocked this claim for its dependence on fig7c-conductivity-drops-10-fold. The verifier pointed out that its reseal and residual parts need only test-pulse data, which the dataset holds, and that the criterion counts those two parts as a partial reproduction; it is now tested. What it takes from fig7c-conductivity-drops-10-fold is the conversion of the test ratio to lm,eff, which needs no conditioning-pulse image; only the part "the cathodic pole is more conductive during the pulse" needs those images, which are not in the dataset, so that part is not tested and the claim can be at most partially reproduced. Under the main reading, full reseal holds; after 570 and 760 V/cm the test response does not differ from control at either pole (unpaired p 0.81 and 0.74 cathodic, 0.64 and 0.098 anodic), though the anodic pole is at 71.2% of control after 760 V/cm. The residual holds; the test response is below 100% of control after 1000, 1200 and 1400 V/cm at both poles (cathodic 57.5%, 25.2%, -11.3%; anodic 79.7%, 68.7%, 48.0%), a test lm,eff of 0.17 and 0.66 mS/m and no finite value at the cathodic pole and 0.057, 0.10 and 0.24 mS/m at the anodic, against 3e-4 mS/m intact. Both hold in 19 of 22 variants; the 3 others are those in which the anodic pole differs from control at 760 V/cm. The part "the test pulse finds no difference between the poles" fails; after 1400 V/cm the cathodic minus anodic normalized test dF is -59.3 points of control (paired p 0.0002; unpaired 0.0015; normalized per cell 0.0056), where the cathodic pole no longer charges; it holds only in the 6 variants that keep the dark frames. Fig. 7C, to which the paper's sentence refers, leaves out the negative cathodic point at 1400 V/cm; with 1400 V/cm left out, a variant, the paired test finds no pole difference at 360 to 1200 V/cm (smallest p 0.12), in 21 of 22 variants. The criterion tests 1400 V/cm; this is asked of a reader (questions/001525.yaml) and does not change the outcome. With trace windows of 6 to 12 px reseal and residual hold; with 4 px they fail (the anodic pole differs at 760 V/cm, p 0.028), and the pole difference at 1400 V/cm is found under every window (paired p 0.0002 to 0.0014). The significance of fig7b-test-pulse-reduced-1200-1400 is reported there (1000 V/cm not significant, as the paper says).
deviations: Same trace, cell, field direction, strength mapping, benchmark, cell count and main reading as fig7a-test-pulse-cosine-up-to-1000.

Normalized test dF for the pole comparison is per-cell dF over the group control of each pole; normalization by each cell's own control is shown as a variant. A standard choice the criterion leaves open; it does not change the result at 1400 V/cm.

outcomes.statement: With 1-us pulses, polarization grows with field strength up to 570 to 780 V/cm; at stronger fields the poles become leaky and show reduced or absent polarization, while regions closer to the equator remain polarized and may exceed the poles.
outcomes.quote: Still stronger electric fields produce a distinct pattern of reduced or absent polarization at the poles (where the membrane becomes too leaky to accumulate the charge) while regions closer to the equator remain relatively intact and may polarize more than the poles
outcomes.notes: Judged on the single-pulse Di-8-ANEPPS escalation of Fig. 4B-C (43 to 1400 V/cm), not in the dataset, which holds only the two-pulse experiment of Fig. 7.

outcomes.statement: FluoVolt dF rises in proportion to field strength until apparent saturation at 66% (255 mV) at 360 V/cm at the cathodic pole and -83% (-320 mV) at 570 V/cm at the anodic pole; stronger fields do not raise it further and lower it at the cathodic pole.
outcomes.quote: ΔF increased proportionally to the electric field strength until reaching apparent saturation at 66% ΔF (255 mV IMP) at 360 V/cm at the cathodic pole, and −83% ΔF (−320 mV IMP) at 570 V/cm at the anodic pole
outcomes.notes: No FluoVolt recording is in the dataset; every file is Di-8-ANEPPS. Dandiset 001526, which names the same paper and is a separate target of the registry, was not used.

outcomes.statement: FluoVolt baseline fluorescence is stable without pulses (no significant bleaching), and the response stays stable through the 60 pulses of each set even at strongly electroporating fields of 1000 V/cm and above.
outcomes.quote: Field strengths of 1000 V/cm and higher caused strong electroporation (see Section 3.5), but the dye response in each set stayed stable through the 60 pulses applied
outcomes.notes: No FluoVolt recording is in the dataset (see fig2a-fluovolt-saturation).

outcomes.statement: Di-8-ANEPPS dF keeps rising up to 570 V/cm at both poles, and responses at 780 V/cm and above decrease gradually within each set of 60 pulses.
outcomes.quote: ΔF kept climbing up to the electric field strength of 570 V/cm at both cell poles ... responses to PEFs at and above 780 V/cm decreased gradually in each set of 60 images
outcomes.notes: The single-pulse Di-8-ANEPPS escalation (43 to 1400 V/cm, n = 5) is not in the dataset.

outcomes.statement: Repeated alternating sets of 150 and 230 V/cm pulses give dF responses that stay constant within and between sets, up to 800 flashes and 480 pulses before the 1000 V/cm exposure.
outcomes.quote: Repeated sets of PEFs at 150 and 230 V/cm, delivered in alternation, produced ΔF responses that stayed constant both within each set and between the sets
outcomes.notes: The alternating 150 and 230 V/cm sets of Fig. 2C-D are not in this dataset. Dandiset 001526, titled as the post-electroporation suitability experiment of the same paper, may hold them; it is a separate target and was not used here.

outcomes.statement: At 1000 V/cm, dF at the cathodic pole declines from 40 +- 10% at the start of the set to 26.6 +- 8% at its end, a trend that is not significant.
outcomes.quote: at an electroporating field strength of 1000 V/cm, ΔF at the cathodic pole decreased from 40 ± 10% at the beginning of the set to 26.6 ± 8% at the end of it. Although not statistically significant (p > 0.05)
outcomes.notes: The Fig. 2C experiment is not in this dataset (see fig2cd-stable-at-150-230).

outcomes.statement: dF averaged over each set stays nearly constant before electroporation but drops by about 20% in the sets acquired after the 1000 V/cm exposure (p < 0.05).
outcomes.quote: ΔF values averaged across each set of 60 PEFs stayed nearly constant before the electroporation, but dropped by about 20% in the sets acquired after it (Fig. 2D, p < 0.05)
outcomes.notes: The Fig. 2C-D experiment is not in this dataset (see fig2cd-stable-at-150-230).

outcomes.statement: Fit through the origin over -150 to +150 mV of calculated IMP, FluoVolt dF changes by 26% and Di-8-ANEPPS by 9.1% per 100 mV, with correlation coefficients 0.96 and 0.78.
outcomes.quote: The correlation coefficients of the fits equaled 0.96 for FluoVolt and 0.78 for Di-8 ANEPPS (due to a lower signal-to-noise ratio), with respective slope coefficients of 26% and 9.1% ΔF per 100 mV of IMP
outcomes.notes: Needs single-pulse recordings with both dyes at 43 to 360 V/cm; none are in the dataset (no FluoVolt file, and Di-8-ANEPPS single pulses only at 50 V). The outside tau fit was not needed.

outcomes.statement: FluoVolt departs from linearity already at +-200 mV of calculated IMP, while Di-8-ANEPPS stays essentially linear from -500 to +500 mV, so the early FluoVolt departure reflects the dye's range and not electroporation.
outcomes.quote: The actual measurements with FluoVolt gradually became non-linear already at ±200 mV, while those for Di-8-ANEPPS stayed essentially linear throughout the tested range from −500 to +500 mV
outcomes.notes: Depends on fig3-dye-calibration-slopes; the recordings are not in the dataset.

outcomes.statement: With FluoVolt, measured and calculated IMP match only at 43 and 150 V/cm; stronger pulses give a maximum dF of 71 +- 10% at the cathodic and -83.5 +- 5% at the anodic pole, and cathodic polarization falls from 71% at 360 V/cm to 45 to 50% at 1000 to 1400 V/cm.
outcomes.quote: this assumption held only for the applied fields of 43 and 150 V/cm, where measured and calculated IMP matched. With stronger PEFs, maximum ΔF reached 71 ± 10% and −83.5 ± 5% at the cathodic and anodic poles, respectively ... polarization at the cathodic pole decreased from 71% at 360 V/cm to 45–50% at 1000–1400 V/cm
outcomes.notes: No FluoVolt recording is in the dataset.

outcomes.statement: With Di-8-ANEPPS, measured IMP falls below the calculated value when the field reaches 570 V/cm, as dF reaches its maximum of 57 +- 14% at the cathodic and -55 +- 4% at the anodic pole, over 600 mV, twice the FluoVolt value.
outcomes.quote: The measured IMP decreased below the calculated value when the electric field reached 570 V/cm, concurrently with reaching the maximum ΔF of 57 ± 14% at the cathodic pole and −55 ± 4% at the anodic pole. These values corresponded to membrane polarization by over 600 mV
outcomes.notes: The single-pulse Di-8-ANEPPS escalation of Fig. 4B is not in the dataset.

outcomes.statement: Averaged over the first 10 of the 60 pulses, cathodic polarization reaches 66 +- 15% (710 +- 200 mV), so the 600-mV maximum over 60 pulses is not the dye limit.
outcomes.quote: Polarization measured this way reached 66 ± 15% (710 ± 200 mV) at the cathodic pole
outcomes.notes: The Fig. 4B experiment is not in the dataset.

outcomes.statement: Above the threshold, pole IMP falls progressively as the field rises, more at the cathodic pole; at 1400 V/cm charging is no longer detectable at the cathodic pole and is about 30% dF (about -330 mV) at the anodic pole.
outcomes.quote: As the electric field increased further, the IMP reached at the poles progressively decreased, and the reduction was more pronounced at the cathodic pole ... At 1400 V/cm, charging was no longer detectable at the cathodic pole (i.e., the membrane became fully permeable) and dropped to ~30% ΔF (~ −330 mV) at the anodic pole
outcomes.notes: The Fig. 4B experiment is not in the dataset.

outcomes.statement: Membrane regions near the equator remain unaffected and follow the cosine dependence predicted by the Schwan equation up to 1000 V/cm, even when the poles are electroporated.
outcomes.quote: appeared relatively unaffected and followed the cosine dependence predicted by Schwan formula up to 1000 V/cm
outcomes.notes: The Fig. 4B-C experiment is not in the dataset.

outcomes.statement: With 0.3-us pulses of 357 to 3320 V/cm imaged at 275 ns, the maximum dF is 53 +- 4% (about 600 mV) at both poles, and the dependence on field strength is like that with 1-us pulses.
outcomes.quote: the maximum ΔF reached was 53 ± 4% (~600 mV) at both cell poles. The pattern of how the response changed with increasing PEF strength was not different from that with 1-μs PEFs either
outcomes.notes: No 0.3-us pulse recording is in the dataset; every file states 1-us pulses.

outcomes.statement: 1 mM Gd3+ extends anodic charging to -864 +- 44 mV against -542 +- 57 mV in controls (p < 0.001), and measured IMP stays nearly equal to calculated IMP down to -780 mV, so the dye response is linear at high IMPs.
outcomes.quote: 1 mM Gd3+ extended the range of membrane charging at the anodic pole down to −864 ± 44 mV (p < 0.001 compared to −542 ± 57 mV in parallel control experiments, Fig. 5A). Furthermore, measured IMP remained nearly identical to the theoretical IMPC down to −780 mV

statistics.n: 7 cells with Gd3+ and 5 control cells

outcomes.notes: No recording with Gd3+ is in the dataset, and the control group of Fig. 5A (single pulses 150 to 1400 V/cm) is not either.

outcomes.statement: At the cathodic pole Gd3+ cells reach 647 +- 44 mV, not significantly more than controls, but Gd3+ prevents the progressive decline of IMP with stronger fields.
outcomes.quote: At the cathodic pole, polarization in the presence of Gd3+ reached 647 ± 44 mV, a value not significantly higher than that in the control group without Gd3+. However, Gd3+ prevented the progressive decline in IMP as the electric field was increased.

statistics.about: Gd3+ against control, datapoints below -700 mV and above 1200 mV of IMPC
statistics.n: 7 cells with Gd3+ and 5 control cells

outcomes.notes: As fig5a-gd-extends-anodic-charging.

outcomes.statement: For most datapoints, Gd3+ reduces the electroporation-induced effective membrane conductivity 2- to 3-fold.
outcomes.quote: For most datapoints, Gd3+ reduced the electroporation ... induced effective conductivity 2–3-fold
outcomes.notes: Needs the Fig. 5A recordings, which are not in the dataset.

outcomes.statement: A single 1-us pulse causes clear Ca2+ entry at 1000 and 1200 V/cm, with the signal elevated through the 5-min observation; the small rise after 780 V/cm is not significant.
outcomes.quote: established a clear peak of Ca2+ entry at 1000 and 1200 ... and Ca2+ signal remained elevated through the 5-min observation period (Fig. 6A). A subtle ΔF increase after exposure at 780 V/cm was at the detection limit and not statistically significant.
outcomes.notes: No Fluo-4 calcium imaging is in the dataset.

outcomes.statement: With trains of 60 1-us pulses at 6 Hz, a strong Ca2+ response occurs in 28% of cells at 780 V/cm and nearly all cells at higher strengths; at 650 V/cm only 2 cells (5.9%) respond strongly, but the mean signal at the end is above zero (p < 0.001) and above that at 230 V/cm (p < 0.05, one-tailed).
outcomes.quote: A strong Ca2+ response was recorded in 28% of cells exposed at 780 V/cm and in nearly all cells at higher intensities (Fig. 6B). At 650 V/cm, only 2 cells (5.9%) showed a strong response, but the mean Ca2+ signal by the end of recording was significantly different from zero (p < 0.001, one sample t-test) and marginally higher than after exposure at 230 V/cm (p < 0.05, single-tailed t-test)
outcomes.notes: No Fluo-4 calcium imaging is in the dataset.

findings.statement: The dandiset holds only the two-pulse Di-8-ANEPPS experiment of Fig. 7A and the bottom panel of Fig. 7B. The FluoVolt, single-pulse escalation, 0.3-us, Gd3+ and Fluo-4 calcium experiments behind Figs. 1 to 6 and the top panel of Fig. 7B are not in it; 22 of the paper's 27 claims cannot be tested here, and one only in part.

Pulses are given in generator volts (50 to 350 V), not in the field strengths (V/cm) the paper reports and computes with Sim4Life, and no mapping is given. The mapping to the Fig. 7A labels (150, 360, 570, 760, 1000, 1200, 1400 V/cm) can only be inferred by rank.
Every file gives the distance between electrodes as 1.00 mm; the paper (Methods 2.2) gives a spacing of 1.6 mm.

The general description shared by every file lists field strengths of 0.15, 0.52, 0.9, 1.27 and 1.57 kV/cm, single pulses at each, and inter-pulse intervals of 1, 5, 25 and 125 us. The files hold single pulses only at 50 V, six conditioning amplitudes (100 to 350 V) and intervals of 1 and 5 us only.

The paper's benchmark for Fig. 7 is a 150 V/cm test pulse after an identical 150 V/cm conditioning pulse (Results 3.7); the files hold no 50 V plus 50 V pair, only a single 50 V pulse, which is the only candidate for the benchmark. Three cells (c4, c5, c6) have two single-pulse files.

Six cells (c5 to c10) have the paper's 5-us interval where Fig. 7 reports n = 5, and nothing says which five were used. Four more cells (c1 to c4) have a 1-us interval, which the paper does not report.

The image series description says exposures began 1 us after the start of recording; the images show the pulse from image 40 (6.7 s at 6 Hz), after 40 baseline images, as Methods 2.3 describe (best split at image 40 in 43 of 73 files, at 39 to 41 in 56).

70 of 73 files have a dark first image (field mean about 209 counts against 276), and 22 more dark images fall elsewhere in the sets; these are images with no laser flash. Nothing in the files marks them. Keeping or dropping them shifts the profile mean dF at the control by 2.17 percentage points under the main, background-subtracted reading (-2.09% kept, -4.26% dropped) and by 1.33 without a background, and the cosine amplitude by 0.0 to 0.3 points; the no-flash level (about 209 counts) shows a camera floor under every image that a dF without background subtraction includes.

The files give no pixel size, no direction of the electric field in image coordinates, and no position of the analysed cell, while each field holds several cells. The field direction can be recovered from the polarization (per-file phases within 6.8 degrees sd).

For the paper's authors, whether a background was subtracted from the potentiometric images and whether images without a laser flash were kept when the 40 baseline and 60 pulse images were collapsed. Background removal doubles the dF scale here (5.6% to 12.6% at 150/150), and only the background-subtracted scale matches the paper's.

The images fade through each set of 100. Over the 40 baseline images the membrane trace intensity (background removed) falls by about 0.10% per image in 43 of 44 files of the 5-us cells, which would predict a uniform dF of -5.16% over the 60 pulse images; the profiles' mean dF is -3.67% over these files and -4.3% at the control, and the two correlate weakly over files (r 0.18). The sign is that of the Di-8-ANEPPS bleaching the paper reports (Results 3.2), the size does not match, and the offset's source is not established; nothing in the files corrects or marks it.

entries.title: Membrane recovery after 1-us electroporation (Semenov et al. 2026)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Semenov et al. (2026) that dandiset 001525 can test. The dandiset holds the two-pulse strobe imaging of ten Di-8-ANEPPS-loaded CHO cells, a conditioning pulse followed by a 150 V/cm test pulse, the experiment of the paper's Fig. 7A and the bottom panel of Fig. 7B. The notebook measures the test-pulse polarization around each cell's perimeter and at its poles, and computes the conductivity calibration of Eq. (2). The other experiments of the paper are not in the dandiset.
